title: event/v1
description: One line of events.jsonl (IC-4): the ordered, append-only, canonical PRIMARY record of a run. Decision records are a materialized view over this stream; on any conflict, events win. Each line is JCS-canonical, individually hashed, and chained (see chain/v1). Timestamps here are REAL UTC epoch-ms: bundles are trusted-side evidence and are not anonymized - only observations are. The payload is a typed union discriminated on `type` (closed enum per major version).

schema.description: Schema name and major version; present per-line because event lines are individually hashed/chained and may be extracted standalone.

seq.description: Monotonic, contiguous, 0-based stream sequence number assigned by the recorder. THE total order; the chain and all tamper-naming key off seq. Gaps or duplicates = verification failure.

ts.description: Virtual-clock time of the event, REAL UTC epoch-milliseconds. For harness-sourced events (EgressBlocked), the harness's copy of the virtual clock at receipt.

turn.description: Decision turn this event belongs to (turn n owns: its observation, responses, gates, next-bar-open fills, and the funding/margin flows of the holding bar), or null for run-scoped events (e.g. EpisodeEnd).

bar_index.description: Decision-bar index at emission, or null for pre/post-episode events.

source.description: Emitting authority - an auditor must know whether the engine or the sandbox proxy witnessed the fact. Multi-party provenance is first-class (a future settlement processor is a new enum member, minor bump).

type.description: Event type; closed V1 vocabulary (dev-plan names kept verbatim, including NearLiquidation added at the C0.3 reconciliation). New members are a minor bump; readers reject unknown types under the same major only if strict-mode, else ignore-with-warning.

payload.description: Type-specific body; validated by the oneOf discriminated union below.

ext.description: Sanctioned extension point (see VERSIONING.md). Engine-ignored, hashed as-is; values are constrained by schema to JCS-safe types with no fractional numbers ($defs/ext_value).

ext_value.description: JCS-safe extension value (DET-2): null, boolean, string, integer within the I-JSON exact range +/-(2^53-1), or arrays/objects of the same, recursively. A JSON number with a fractional part (e.g. 1.5) is schema-INVALID here - ext contents ride into hashed documents as-is, and no fractional number may enter a hashed document. Boundary note: JSON Schema's 'integer' type admits a mathematically-integral literal such as 1.0; the CI instance scan (float-rejecting JSON parse, see VERSIONING.md) closes that remaining lexical gap.

anyOf.description: JSON string (decimal values ride as strings, e.g. '0.7').
Integer within the I-JSON exact range (JCS round-trips it byte-identically).
Object whose values are all JCS-safe.

additionalProperties.description: Signed target leverage in 1e-4 units (15000 = 1.5x long, -15000 = 1.5x short, 0 = flat).

target_lev_map.description: Canonical parsed target vector: market alias -> integer leverage in 1e-4 units. The only action representation that is ever hashed.

ObservationEmitted.description: Turn start: binds the stored observation into the chain (WHAT THE AGENT SAW). Emitted once per turn even when a retry re-sends the identical observation.

observation_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the JCS bytes of the observation served this turn (equals the hash of observations/NNNN.json).

observation_ref.description: Bundle-relative path of the stored observation, e.g. 'observations/0007.json'.

AgentResponded.description: Each response received, including malformed ones (WHAT THE AGENT SAID). Raw text is content-addressed into raw/ rather than inlined, so share-profile redaction can delete the blob without breaking any chained record hash (SCH-3 x SCH-4).

attempt.description: 1 = first ask; 2 = the single retry after a validation failure.

raw_ref.description: Bundle-relative path of the verbatim response bytes, e.g. 'raw/0007-a1.txt'.

raw_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the verbatim response bytes; survives redaction (verifiable absence).

raw_bytes.description: Byte length of the verbatim response.

latency_ms.description: Harness-measured wall latency, request-sent to last-byte-received. Recorded, never consumed by any economic computation (outside the determinism domain).

http_status.description: HTTP status code of the response; null for in-process adapters.

token_usage.description: Agent-self-reported token usage copied from action.usage; null when unavailable (explicit null, never absent).

ActionParsed.description: Parse success (WHAT THE AGENT MEANT): the canonical integer form of the wire action. Free-text comment and usage telemetry are NOT copied here - they live in the content-addressed raw response. The leverage payload (target_lev_1e4, max_slippage_bps) is conditionally required behind intent_kind via the allOf/if/then above - the same seam as the wire form (action.v1). Because intent_kind is itself required here and its sole v1 member is 'leverage_target', every v1 canonical action still carries the full leverage vector (no behavior or byte change for trading); a future intent kind (e.g. commerce purchase_intent) adds its own enum member + conditional branch + optional payload properties - a MINOR bump on this hashed form, not an event/v2 major.

intent_kind.description: Canonical intent discriminator (the IC-3 seam): constant 'leverage_target' for every v1 trading action (wire absence canonicalizes to it), so it never varies within v1 and determinism is unaffected. On the additive-tolerant list (VERSIONING.md): a future intent kind (commerce purchase_intent) is a new enum member whose payload branch carries its own canonical fields - a MINOR bump instead of an action/v2 + event/v2 + chain-rippling major.

target_lev_1e4.description: Canonical signed target-leverage vector (see $defs/target_lev_map); conditionally required behind intent_kind = leverage_target (always present in v1).

max_slippage_bps.description: Slippage tolerance in integer bps; null when the agent omitted it (wire absence canonicalizes to null).

from_attempt.description: Which IC-6 attempt produced the accepted action.

ActionRejected.description: No valid action this turn after all attempts: parse/transport failure or timeout. Position unchanged - a rejection is data, not a crash (SAFE-2). Gate blocks are NOT rejections; they are RiskCheck{block} on a successfully parsed action.

reason.description: Final failure reason (of the last attempt), from the IC-3 validation table. timeout = no bytes within the deadline; agent_error = transport failure/crash/5xx. Both are missed decisions (SAFE-4).

detail.description: Deterministic human-readable diagnostic template instantiated with the offending values.

validator_error.description: The exact validator error text fed back to the agent on the retry (attempt 2), or null if no retry occurred - the audit answer to 'was it warned?'.

attempts.description: How many attempts were made (timeout/agent_error are never retried, so those record 1).

RiskCheck.description: One conformance verdict for one constraint (WHICH RULES RAN). Emitted for EVERY active constraint whenever an action is parsed - pass AND block both recorded (SAFE-1 attempted-vs-executed). Any block => the whole action is blocked, position unchanged, never clamped.

constraint_type.description: Constraint semantics (closed V1 enum, minor-bump extensible).

observed.description: The value checked (e.g. requested gross leverage, projected turnover), in `unit` units.

limit.description: The limit in force, in `unit` units.

verdict.description: The conformance verdict. This enum is on the additive-tolerant list (VERSIONING.md): a future third outcome (e.g. step_up / requires_user_authorization for commerce mandate flows) arrives as a minor bump, not a major. observed/limit are deliberately numeric-only in v1; a non-scalar conformance value (e.g. an observed merchant vs an allowed set) arrives as an optional additive payload field (minor bump) - documented seam, IC-4 design decision 9.

OrderFilled.description: Next-bar-open execution (WHAT HAPPENED), with the fill price fully decomposed so 'why this price' is answerable without the engine. The stress_2x economic path is a stored re-simulation (ledger_stress_2x.jsonl), not a second event stream.

market.description: Market alias (resolve to venue instrument via the pack manifest).

requested_qty_base_1e8.description: Quantity requested by the target-delta, 1e-8 base units, before caps/rounding.

qty_base_1e8.description: Quantity actually filled, 1e-8 base units (rounded toward zero to qty_step; capped by participation).

ref_open_px_ticks.description: Reference price: the next bar's trade-series open, ticks.

half_spread_ticks.description: Worst-side half-spread applied, in ticks (agent-adverse rounding).

impact_ticks.description: Impact term applied, in ticks (agent-adverse rounding).

fill_px_ticks.description: Effective fill price = ref_open +/- (half_spread + impact) against the taker, ticks.

notional_micro.description: Fill notional = qty x fill price, micro-quote.

fee_micro.description: Taker fee charged, micro-quote, rounded up (agent-adverse).

slippage_1e8.description: (fill_px - ref_open)/ref_open signed, in 1e-8 units (1 bp = 10000; bps derivable exactly). Compared against the agent's max_slippage_bps x 10000.

cost_profile.description: Cost profile of this event stream. Always 'primary'; the stress profile is a stored ledger re-simulation (MATH-5).

OrderCancelled.description: Whole or partial cancellation. A participation-cap partial produces one OrderFilled (filled part) AND one OrderCancelled (excess) in the same turn; excess is never filled later (MATH-7).

reason.description: Why: exceeded participation cap; below min notional; modeled slippage above the agent's max_slippage_bps; or quantity rounded to zero at qty_step.

cancelled_qty_base_1e8.description: Quantity cancelled (the whole request, or the excess over the cap), 1e-8 base units.

detail.description: Deterministic structured diagnostic (e.g. cap value, bar volume, computed slippage) rendered from a fixed template.

FundingApplied.description: One venue settlement stamp crossed while holding (COST TO HOLD). Notional = position x INDEX price x rate - index, never mark or trade (MATH-4); the three-series separation is visible in the record itself.

rate_1e8.description: Settled rate in 1e-8 units, era cap applied; positive = longs pay.

position_qty_base_1e8.description: Signed position held through the settlement, 1e-8 base units.

amount_micro.description: Signed funding flow, micro-quote; negative = agent paid (agent-adverse rounding on the division).

MarginUpdate.description: Margin state per market: emitted at every bar close while a position is open, and after every fill, funding application, and liquidation. Fully specifies the dev-plan's '{...}' placeholder. min_intrabar_dist_to_liq records the closest approach on the wick - near-death evidence even when the close was safe.

mark_px_ticks.description: Mark-price close of the bar, ticks (margin/uPnL/liquidation all price off mark).

mark_high_ticks.description: Mark-series intra-bar high, ticks (short-side liquidation check input, MATH-3).

mark_low_ticks.description: Mark-series intra-bar low, ticks (long-side liquidation check input, MATH-3).

entry_px_ticks.description: Volume-weighted entry price, ticks; null when flat.

maintenance_margin_micro.description: Maintenance margin required at current notional and tier, micro-quote.

liq_px_ticks.description: Liquidation trigger price, ticks; null when flat.

dist_to_liq_1e8.description: |mark_close - liq_px|/mark_close in 1e-8 units (floor); null when flat.

min_intrabar_dist_to_liq_1e8.description: Minimum distance-to-liquidation reached on the bar's mark wick, 1e-8 units; null when flat. The near-miss number.

NearLiquidation.description: The holding bar's adverse mark extreme came within the near-liquidation threshold (5% in V1) of the liquidation price WITHOUT crossing it (a cross emits LiquidationTriggered instead). Feeds the near-death timeline (C5.1); added to IC-4 at the C0.3 reconciliation.

trigger.description: Which mark extreme approached: high threatens shorts, low threatens longs.

mark_extreme_px_ticks.description: The adverse mark extreme of the bar (low for longs, high for shorts), ticks.

liq_px_ticks.description: The liquidation trigger price that was approached, ticks.

min_intrabar_dist_to_liq_1e8.description: Closest approach: |extreme - liq_px| / extreme as a 1e-8 fraction (floor). Below threshold_1e8 by construction of this event.

LiquidationTriggered.description: Intra-bar mark high/low breached the liquidation price (including gap-through). Terminal: the episode ends after bookkeeping (MATH-3).

trigger.description: Which mark extreme breached: high liquidates shorts, low liquidates longs.

liq_px_ticks.description: The liquidation trigger price that was crossed, ticks.

close_px_ticks.description: Forced-close execution price: the CONSERVATIVE side of the triggering bar, ticks.

penalty_micro.description: Liquidation penalty charged on liquidated notional, micro-quote.

loss_micro.description: Total realized loss of the liquidation including penalty, micro-quote (negative = loss).

KillSwitchTriggered.description: Episode drawdown limit (20%) breached: engine force-flattens all positions and keeps observing; further non-flat targets are blocked and recorded (SAFE-3).

drawdown_1e8.description: Peak-to-current NAV drawdown fraction in 1e-8 units at trigger.

flatten_order_seqs.description: seq numbers of the forced flattening OrderFilled events (ordinary fills, referenced not duplicated).

PostKillSwitchAttempt.description: A non-flat target arrived after the kill switch fired. The attempt itself is discipline evidence (SAFE-1/SAFE-3), recorded alongside its RiskCheck{drawdown-ks, block}.

target_lev_1e4.description: The attempted (blocked) signed target-leverage vector (see $defs/target_lev_map) - the violation itself is evidence.

raw_sha256.description: Content address of the verbatim response that carried the attempt.

EgressBlocked.description: The sandbox refused a network egress attempt from the agent container (ISO-2). source = 'harness'. Reports flag these as safety events.

destination.description: Destination as observed: domain, DNS name, or IP literal.

port.description: Destination port; null when not applicable (e.g. DNS query name block).

protocol.description: Protocol class of the refused attempt.

count.description: Coalesced repeat count of identical attempts within the turn.

EpisodeEnd.description: Always the last event of a complete stream - the in-band completeness sentinel: a stream without EpisodeEnd is truncated (SCH-3).

reason.description: completed = window exhausted; liquidated = terminal liquidation; aborted = operator/pre-flight abort before or during the run.

final_turn.description: Last decision-turn index, or null if aborted before turn 0.
